purpose: library: the purchase of Alaska — a dated diplomatic chronology (Peter the Great dispatches Vitus Bering in 1725; Russia offers to sell in 1859; the Civil War delays; Secretary of State William Seward agrees with Russian Minister Edouard de Stoeckl on March 30, 1867 to purchase Alaska for $7.2 million; the Senate approves April 9; President Andrew Johnson signs May 28; formal transfer October 18, 1867), three decades of military/naval/Treasury rule, civil government in 1884, 'Seward's Folly' vindicated by the 1896 Yukon gold discovery, World War II strategic recognition, and statehood on January 3, 1959 — with the 'fewer than four hundred' permanent Russian settlers detail. Fits timeline ordering and quiz cards with predict-then-reveal on dates and the price.
